q: How does a page decide whether its frontmatter or the generated seo metadata wins in nimpress?
a: Decided by the user on 2026-09-04: an override boolean inside the frontmatter meta object. Generated values from seo.auto fill every field the page leaves empty; with meta.override true the authored fields beat the generated ones, and without it the generated values beat the authored ones for the fields the generator produces. The config sets the initial value per page, the frontmatter holds the override.

q: Which framework can a custom nimpress page type be written in?
a: Svelte only, decided by the user on 2026-09-04. A pageTypes block in the config maps a type name to a Svelte component file; a new name registers a type and an existing name replaces the built in renderer. No iframe route for other frameworks and no second runtime in the app.

q: How does a page join a sidebar section without changing its url in nimpress?
a: The sidebar tree in buildSidebar in src/plugin.ts is keyed by url segments, and a sidebar block with a path replaces the page's parent segment with that path, so sidebar name Setup with path setup lands the page on the same node as the physical docs/setup folder and the two merge. The docs tree laid on 2026-09-03 uses this: root pages keep their urls and declare their section, new pages live in the section folders, and only the extensions folder moved to authoring because a two segment url nests a declared group under its folder instead of replacing it.

q: How does the sly-svelte-location-router in nimpress treat an unknown route?
a: It matches by prefix: resolveRoute in node_modules/sly-svelte-location-router tests only the first N segments of the url against each route, so an unknown deep path renders the nearest parent page with leftover segments and the fallback prop never fires. The resolvedRoute store holds the full path, not a leftover flag. nimpress therefore renders the 404 page from the generated page template in src/plugin.ts when the current path is not a key of manifest.byPath, and the fallback prop only covers paths outside the base.

q: Why did a hash on an in app link vanish right after navigation in nimpress?
a: The router keeps the previous page component mounted under the new route key while the next page loads, so the old page's hash spy in src/framework/hashSpy.ts started with the new path and old content, saw its first heading below the top after the scroll reset, and stripped the hash. Fixed on 2026-09-03: the spy captures its pathname, returns when the location left it, and clears only a hash it wrote itself through the owned flag. Reproduced with the scratch race spec under parallel workers and covered by e2e/tags.spec.ts.

q: Which names do the nimpress docs keep when a definition sentence is borrowed from a reference?
a: Decided by the user on 2026-09-03: borrowed definition sentences keep their wording but nimpress names stay. Callouts stay callouts and nothing is called admonitions, actions stay actions, cards and features stay, frontmatter stays one word. The docs page skeleton is a definition paragraph then Configuration, Usage, Customization, written into .claude/rules/docs-authoring.md under Page skeleton.

q: Does nimpress adopt a dotted features flag array for its switches?
a: No. Decided by the user on 2026-09-03: every switch is a config field in NimpressUserConfig in src/types.ts or a frontmatter field in the schema in src/plugin.ts, never a dotted flag array. The docs map each behavior to its field, and a missing behavior is added as a field. The 2.4.0 release added them that way: hide and status, tabs, images, icons, math, announce, footer, repo, feedback, tags, seo.
